precepts.text: Give me neither poverty nor riches; lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain. He put his spirit in us; we are a holy people. When they say you cannot keep the commandments, that is because they want to remain in their sins. That does not mean we have never sinned; if anybody says they have not sinned, they lie.
precepts.point: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. What we just read was the first four commandments, and they go into loving the Lord thy God. All of this blending of religions is meant to take you away from serving the Lord thy God. How many of these religions honor the Sabbath day? How many of these Christians are going to keep the feast of tabernacles, the feast of weeks, the Passover? It is meant to keep you in sin.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.” To see what that means, go to Proverbs.

“Two things have I required of thee; deny me them not before I die: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.”

Lest I be full and deny thee: that is one way of taking his name in vain. Lest I be poor and steal: that is sin, and sinning while bearing his name is taking the name of my God in vain. We are called by his name; he says we are a holy people, and he put his spirit in us.

So when they say you cannot keep the commandments, why can’t we? That does not mean we have never sinned. All men have sinned, and if anybody says they have not sinned, they lie. But when they say you cannot keep the commandments, it is because they want to remain in their sins.

This sits inside the first four commandments, which go into loving the Lord thy God. All of this blending of religions is meant to take you away from serving him and to keep you in sin.

precepts.text: The way of an adulterous woman: she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness. The song's line about loving an eater is this same characteristic.
precepts.point: Sisters should not be doing dances they see online. The 'eating' motion in the popular challenge is not about food, and the deacon takes the class to Proverbs to show what it actually describes.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.why:
“Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.” If you love this place, the love of the Father is not in you. The state of mind of a saint is, I want to be up out of here; I hate this place. All that is in the world is “the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life”, and the lust of the eyes today is TikTok and social media, where the minds of a lot of young brothers and sisters are.

There is a challenge everybody is doing, a dance where they act like they are eating something. The song is called feeling on my body, and it is all about sex. Young brothers and sisters, even among us, watch it and mimic it, and some school sisters were doing that dumb, stupid dance on the new moon. When she says she loves an eater, you think she is talking about eating food? She ain't talking about eating food. She's talking about eating sausage.

The scripture shows what it is: “Such is the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.” She eats and wipes her mouth, and then says she has done no wickedness. That is the characteristic of an adulterous, wicked woman, and that is what the dance is about: sucking rod.

So sisters, you should not be doing those dances. You don't even understand what's behind them. It is the lust of the eyes: you see it on social media and think it's cool. It isn't innocent; you are conjuring demons. We are supposed to be separate, not following the things we see in the world, because the world passeth away, and the lust thereof, “but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.”

precepts.text: The conies are but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks.
precepts.point: Their carcase shall ye not touch sits inside the dietary law: it goes into sacrificing the unclean thing and eating it, touching it with the mouth. It does not mean a dead animal in your path cannot be moved out of the way with the hands; the tabernacle itself had to be built by hand with badgers' skins.

note.label: Leviticus 11: The Dietary Law of Clean and Unclean Beasts

precepts.why:
“The conies are but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks.” Solomon describes the same animal as the psalm: small, feeble, and living among the rocks. That is the pika, the coney of Leviticus 11:5.

Knowing the animal settles the matter. It “cheweth the cud, but divideth not the hoof”, one mark and not the other, so it is unclean to you. Leave it alone, as with the camel, the hare and the swine.

precepts.text: Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.
precepts.point: From the beginning the Most High commanded the prophets to speak his words and diminish not a word: do not be afraid to tell the nations what the scripture actually says, that salvation is to Israel and that there is no female deity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.” Adding to the word sounds like god loves everybody: how many have been found liars saying it?

Do not quote what the Most High has not said. An opinion off the top of your head cannot be proven by scripture, and the one who adds it to his words is reproved and found a liar. That is the weight behind “Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you”.

precepts.text: Remove far from me vanity and lies; give me neither poverty nor riches; lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.
precepts.point: Solomon's prayer is the humble spirit: give me neither poverty nor riches, feed me with food convenient for me. Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and money has pulled people out of this walk; poverty drives a man to steal. The chief things for life are simple, water, bread, clothing, and an house to cover shame, and the Most High blessed Solomon with riches because riches were not his god.

note.label: Deuteronomy 5: The Ten Commandments Reiterated

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain” is not about saying oh my god. Solomon shows how the name is taken in vain: “lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.” Breaking the commandments, stealing, lying, bearing false witness, committing adultery, is how the name is taken in vain.

Solomon's prayer is the humble spirit: “Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord?” Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and money has pulled people out of this walk; poverty drives a man to steal. The Most High blessed Solomon with riches because riches were not his god.

precepts.text: Give me neither poverty nor riches, lest I be full and deny thee, or lest I be poor and steal and take the name of my God in vain.
precepts.point: Why? Because the devil, with the permission of the Lord, was able to put his hand on Job to try him. That is what we need as Israelites; when we do certain things the Lord gives us certain things, and He has to try them to see if the heart is still going to be the same way.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

precepts.why:
“Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.” Riches can make a man full and deny the Lord; poverty can make him steal and take God's name in vain. Either one tries the heart.

Job had the riches, and in one day it all went. The Sabeans took the oxen and slew the servants; the fire of God burned up the sheep and the servants; the Chaldeans made out three bands and carried away the camels; a great wind from the wilderness smote the four corners of the house and it fell upon the young men. Job just lost his cattle, his servants, and his children. Job just lost everything.

Why? Because the devil, with the permission of the Lord, was able to put his hand on Job to try him. That is what we need as Israelites: when we do certain things the Lord gives us certain things, and he has to try them to see if the heart is still going to be the same way, full or poor.

precepts.text: Two types of people: those that are full deny the Most High and say who is the Lord, and those with too little steal and take His name in vain.
precepts.point: They set their mouth against the heavens and their tongue walks through the earth.

note.label: Psalm 73: God Is Good to Israel

precepts.why:
Psalm 73 describes the wicked who prosper: “Their eyes stand out with fatness: they have more than heart could wish.” They have abundance, more than they need, and “pride compasseth them about as a chain”. They wear their pride because they think no hurt can come to them. The entertainers, rappers and people in Congress live luxurious lives and no harm comes to them.

Proverbs shows why that fatness is dangerous: “Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.”

Two types of people: those that are full deny the Most High and say who is the Lord, and those with too little steal and take his name in vain. The full ones are the ones of Psalm 73 who “set their mouth against the heavens” and “speak wickedly concerning oppression”, speaking loftily and proudly. Our people do not believe they are oppressed; some say there is no racism and the world is equal. Better to be fed with food convenient for you than to be so full you deny the Lord.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: For a servant when he reigneth. So a servant when he reigns. Who is reigning the earth today? Servants. That is why the scriptures say the earth is turned upside down. The rightful owners of the earth are not ruling. And is there peace in the earth? Absolutely not.
And a fool when he is filled with meat.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: For an odious woman when she is married. Odious: deserving or causing hatred, hateful, detestable. But she is probably married because she looked good, and she has all these qualities about her. Look at some of the synonyms: execrable, despicable, objectionable, abominable. And if those are too hard to understand, look at the antonyms, the opposite: lovable, attractive. So she is not lovable, and that is not the physical attraction. That goes back to Peter's — that is the inner woman.
So that odious woman when she is married, she is going to disquiet the earth even. That is the housetop it is better to be on, than with that contentious woman.
